items.summary: Recommendation: keep SearchWoot private. Woot API access is documented, but commercial/public display, storage, derivatives, alerts, and monetization rights are unconfirmed; counsel review and owner authorization remain required before outreach. Ordinary reversible growth may continue within existing consent, disclosure, claims, and affiliate boundaries.

Risk disposition: blocked for SearchWoot public beta or full launch; conditional for ordinary reversible fleet growth. The API access mechanism is evidenced, but public/commercial storage, derivatives, display, alerts, affiliate use, and advertising rights are not. Human counsel is required for upstream rights, privacy jurisdiction treatment, notification data, vendor/DPA terms, and any monetization expansion. Fleet compliance is a technical baseline, not certification: 36 sites pass, 17 fail, and 6 are unknown. Do not treat incomplete telemetry as a growth blocker where existing consent, disclosures, data handling, claims, copyright/trademark, platform-policy, and affiliate boundaries are preserved. No legal launch task is closed. Next evidence action: attach the authoritative permission/terms record or obtain owner authorization to send the prepared written request to the upstream provider; keep the site private until all legal and non-legal gates are satisfied.

Launch-readiness progress: source-rights, data-flow/retention, analytics-consent, and logs/vendor/incident tasks remain open because required evidence is incomplete. Existing evidence confirms official API documentation, but not redistribution rights; repository/configuration evidence is partial; privacy and GA4 evidence is incomplete; security, accuracy/freshness, measurement, and owner gates remain blocked. The exact decision is keep_private. Do not send external requests, expand alerts, enable new tracking, monetize, or change launch status without owner authorization and human counsel where identified.
